summary.intent: Use the GSD manager workflow to dashboard-manage CipherBox milestone v2.0: verify phase 70.1, diagnose dashboard status anomalies, and drive the remaining closeout phases (74-79) through plan+execute, working autonomously across multiple quota-limited sessions.
summary.outcome: Phase 70.1 was verified (SC#6 live crash-resume suite passed 6/6 after fixing a stale API process and a missing test-login secret) and marked complete; a GSD plan-scanner bug that falsely showed Phase 69 as 'Executing' was root-caused and fixed (file rename) and both changes shipped via PR #606. Phases 74 and 75 were subsequently planned, executed, and verified (74 code-verified pending CI-gated legs; 75 fully verified/complete) using a corrected sequential main-checkout-per-feat-branch method after worktree-based background planning proved unworkable; Phase 77 planning/execution was still in progress when the session ended.

repo: GSD manager dashboard's `is_active` flag just means 'a file in the phase dir was modified in the last 5 minutes' — not an actual running-agent check; recently-edited but idle phase dirs render as falsely active.

`phase uat-passed --require-verification` downgrades disk_status to `partial` when implementation is complete and verification passed but no `<N>-UAT.md` exists — phases verified via CI/cargo (not human UAT) need a minimal UAT stub to read as Complete on the dashboard.

sdk-e2e vitest harness does not load `.env` — `SDK_E2E_SECRET` must be exported into the shell before running, else it falls back to a different default secret than the API's `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET` and every test 401s (looks like a code failure, isn't).

The local API dev process on :3000 can silently be a stale `node dist/main.js` from hours earlier, serving old compiled code with a mismatched `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET` — always confirm the running process is source-built before trusting live-stack test results.
`commit.gpgsign=false` in this repo, so autonomous/background commits don't block on 1Password biometric prompts.

Pre-commit hooks (lint-staged) in this monorepo are slow (~1-2 min); a Bash commit call that appears to hang or time out has usually already landed — verify via `git log` rather than assuming failure or retrying.
The gsd commit helper occasionally false-negatives `commit_failed` while the commit actually landed on disk.

code.finding: Loose fallback matcher counts any `.md` file whose name merely contains the case-insensitive substring 'PLAN' (not just `*-PLAN.md`) as a plan file — miscounted `69-WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md` ('write-PLANE') as a 26th plan, causing `implementation_complete: false` and a false 'Executing' dashboard status.
`is_active` is computed purely from 'was a file in this phase dir modified in the last 5 minutes', not from any live-process/agent check.

workflow: A background sub-agent launched at the repo root cannot `EnterWorktree` into a pre-existing worktree ('repo root, not an isolated worktree') — this breaks the pattern of spawning parallel worktree-isolated planners and later resuming them individually.

The working alternative for multi-phase autonomous planning/execution: switch the MAIN checkout to each phase's `feat/*` branch sequentially and run one background agent per phase inheriting that cwd/branch, rather than parallel worktrees — avoids the EnterWorktree limitation and shared-DB/stack contention.

CronCreate one-shot jobs can carry detailed resume instructions (exact working method, current progress, hard rules) to autonomously continue multi-hour agent work across session quota resets; instructions should be corrected/re-issued if the working method changes mid-session.

Task/agent completion notifications can reflect a stale mid-run checkpoint message rather than true final state (especially on quota-kill) — always verify actual on-disk git state (commits, branches, files) before trusting an agent's self-reported summary.

friction: All three background planners (74, 75, 77) died mid-run from hitting the session quota limit before committing plans or finishing, requiring disk-state reassessment and relaunch each time.
EnterWorktree failed when trying to resume background planning agents in their existing worktrees, wasting an agent invocation and forcing a pivot to sequential main-checkout-per-branch.

A stale, differently-configured API process caused a false-negative crash-resume test result (401) that initially looked like a Phase 70.1 code defect, requiring multi-step diagnosis (process ID, secrets, restart).
Even after restarting the API from source, tests still 401'd because vitest doesn't load `.env` — a second, distinct false-negative requiring further diagnosis.

The dashboard falsely showed Phase 69 as 'Executing' for two unrelated reasons in sequence (missing UAT artifact, then a plan-count scanner bug), requiring iterative root-causing before the real bug was found.
The Phase 75 planning/execution agent self-stalled in an internal background-wait loop and returned early without finishing, wasting a session-quota window.

Uncommitted plan drafts were left at risk multiple times when quota cutoffs killed agents before a commit landed (Phase 74's 7 draft plans, Phase 77's 10 draft plans), requiring manual `git add`/commit recovery on resume.
A harness-reported rustc E0277 compile error for Phase 75 required an extra manual `cargo check --workspace` to confirm it was a stale rust-analyzer artifact rather than a real regression.
open_items: Phase 74: two CI-gated verification legs remain open (Windows compile of WinFsp code; 3-platform desktop-e2e matrix) — recorded in 74-UAT.md, phase not marked complete pending CI run.
Phase 77: plan-checker/execution still in progress at transcript end.
Phases 76, 78, 79 not yet planned or executed.
Feat branches for 74, 75, 77 (and pending 76/78/79) are not yet merged or opened as PRs — left ready for user review, per no-direct-to-main rule.
A follow-up safety-net cron resume was scheduled for the next quota reset (~14:45) in case the 77/76/78/79 work gets cut off again.
Previously-known open gap (from memory): SHARE-WRITE-KEY write-share key threading is still unresolved and wasn't addressed this session.
